correctness.rationale: Partition token vertices into A-A, B-B, A-B classes. For arbitrary chosen D, let A₀,B₀ be vertices not incident with selected cross pairs and C_A,C_B vertices covered by same-side selected pairs. All A-A or B-B token vertices are dominated exactly when every pair from the corresponding zero-degree set lies in D_A or D_B. All cross tokens are dominated exactly when every pair in (A\C_A)×(B\C_B) lies in D_X. With k=|B₀|, x≥n−k and z≥C(k,2), hence x+z≥n−1; a set of size <n fails in equality cases k=1,2. With exactly n selected tokens, y=|D_A|≤1. When y=1, k=2 and the entire form is Family I. When y=0, the cross-coverage inequalities show all B vertices belong to some selected B-pair, force k=2 and n≤4, exclude n=3, and leave n=4 with two disjoint B-pairs and an injection of two B-indices into A. Count families and group orbits. Independently exhaustively enumerated all n-vertex candidate dominating subsets for n=3,4,5 and reproduced 9,54,30 with all examples belonging to these families. This is not an infinite computational proof.
